blocks.text:
Primary Schools enrolling secondary students negotiate payment arrangements directly with the SIDE Manager Business Operations. The default position is that SIDE invoices the school.

These contributions are payable annually at the beginning of the school year, or at the time of enrolment. Please refer to the Extra Cost Options form to determine payment amounts.

tabs.label: High School, Senior High School & Colleges
tabs.title: Government Schools

blocks.text: The public school sector costs are:
Senior high schools, high schools and agricultural colleges

Senior high schools, high schools and agricultural colleges with Year 11 and 12 students enrolled in subjects through SIDE are required by DoE to contribute funds to access those courses. Based on the assumption that the full load for a Year 11 and 12 student is, on average five (5) year long courses, each course being studied through SIDE has been determined as 0.2 FTE of a student load.

School enrolments will be cross referenced with SIDE data following the Semester 1 Census. The school contribution is based on 0.014 teacher FTE per student subject at the endorsed notional salary rate for a teacher. Adjustments for these amounts will be made to one line budgets.
In 2026 this contribution will be $1981.33 per student/per course. Please note that this amount CANNOT be passed onto parents/caregivers.
All non-government school student registrations through SIDE, including Curriculum and Reengagement Education Schools, are to be charged at the full recovery rate.

items.label: Mathematics, English, Science and Humanities, Social Sciences

blocks.text: District High Schools and Remote Community Schools will be invoiced for the learning area and course costs for each student enrolment.
Primary Schools enrolling secondary students negotiate payment arrangements directly with the SIDE Manager Business Operations.
The default position is that SIDE invoices the school.

Participation arrangements under section 24 of the Education Act 1999 enable students to be provided educational programs from SIDE as a service provider to the school. Schools are charged depending on their category.
All non-government school student registrations through SIDE are to be charged at the full recovery rate.

sections.title: Booklist
sections.lead: The booklist is a curated compilation of all resources students need for the term.
sections.body:
Subject-specific workbooks to guide lessons, specialised materials such as calculators or other course-required tools, and essential stationery — paperclips, staplers, paper punches, rulers, pens, pencils, writing paper and folders — for organising and completing assignments.

Resources for all year groups can be sourced from any supplier, or you can utilise our own.

sections.title: Financial Aid
sections.lead: Students learning through distance education may be eligible for financial assistance.

tabs.label: Assistance for Isolated Children Scheme
tabs.title: Assistance for Isolated Children Scheme
tabs.lead: A group of payments for parents and carers of children who can't go to a local government school because of geographical isolation, disability or special needs.

blocks.text:
Your child needs to be studying full time. They must be doing primary, secondary or other approved study.

You may get Assistance for Isolated Children if your child does approved full time tertiary study because they don’t have access to a state secondary school.
Your child must also meet at least one of the following isolation conditions:

items: Have no reasonable access to a school.

tabs.label: Secondary Assistance Scheme
tabs.title: Secondary Assistance Scheme
tabs.lead: The Western Australian Department of Education provides an allowance to assist eligible families with secondary schooling costs.

blocks.text: To be eligible for the allowance the parent/guardian must hold a Services Australia (Centrelink) or Veterans’ Affairs card that represents a statement of income for the family.
The allowance consists of two components:

items: **$300** Clothing Allowance paid directly to the parent/guardian or the school.
**$235** Educational Program Allowance paid directly to the school.

blocks.text: Application is made by the parent or guardian for student/s enrolled in Years 7–12 studying a full time secondary course.
